title: Runtime dispatch arbitration for per-request quant profiles (FP16/FP8/INT8)
creator: Maya Chen
description: Design and implement a runtime arbitration layer that selects and dispatches the most appropriate kernel path (FP16/FP8/INT8) on a per-request basis using quantization profiles and lightweight on-device calibration checks. Focus on minimizing end-to-end latency regressions while keeping model quality within defined accuracy budgets. The work includes a scoring heuristic, integration with offline calibration artifacts, safety-fallbacks, telemetry, and a test harness for accuracy validation against golden prompt sets.
acceptance_criteria: Runtime can select FP16/FP8/INT8 kernel per request using quant-profile metadata and a lightweight decision heuristic
End-to-end median latency increase <= 5% relative to FP16 baseline under standard-serving load
Quality regression <= 0.7% absolute on the golden prompt accuracy set compared to pinned FP16 baseline
Automated calibration artifacts (per-model quant profiles) are consumed during startup and validated against stored calibration checksums
Fallback policy triggers to FP16 or previous safe variant within 250ms of detecting accuracy drift or kernel failure
E2E integration tests and perf benchmarks added to CI and gated for rollout
implementation_steps: Define quant-profile schema extension: add per-layer dynamic range hints, calibration sample stats, and timestamps
Implement scoring heuristic: utility = w_accuracy*delta_quality - w_latency*delta_latency - w_cost*estimated_cost
Build a lightweight calibration checker that runs N sample tokens on cold start and periodically in low QPS windows
Add dispatch arbiter in runtime that picks kernel path and attaches decision metadata to traces
Implement soft-fallback and circuit-breaker: track moving accuracy estimate and revert to safer path on threshold breach
Expose telemetry: per-request kernel_choice, decision_score, calibration_check_pass/fail, fallback_reason
Add unit and integration tests for dispatch logic and fallback behavior
Benchmark mixed-precision paths across target hardware matrix and collect profiles for default weights
test_plan: Golden prompt set: 2k prompts across summarization, completion, instruction tasks; store expected outputs for exact-match and n-gram metrics
Calibration datasets: small sample (1k), medium (10k) and full (100k) used in offline quant profile generation
Metrics to monitor: EM, BLEU, ROUGE-L, perplexity delta, token-level logit deviation, tail latency (p99)
A/B tests: compare policy-enabled runtime vs pinned-FP16 baseline on a synthetic production-like replay load
Stress tests: high-concurrency scenarios to validate batching interactions and to catch jitter introduced by arbitration
Drift injection tests: purposely corrupt quant-profile or simulate mismatched calibration to verify fallback triggers
rollout_plan: Guarded feature flag: runtime.arbiter.quant_profiles (off by default)
Canary rollout: 1% traffic -> 5% -> 25% -> 100% with automated metric gates
Mesh of canaries across zones and hardware types (A100, H100, upcoming AmpereNext) to catch HW-specific regressions
Automated rollback triggers: quality_regression > 1.0% absolute on golden set OR p99 latency increase > 20%
Post-rollout 48h monitoring checklist: cost per token, per-route accuracy, fallback rate, calibration check failure rate
notes: We prefer per-model quant profiles created by existing calibration pipeline; if missing, runtime will default to FP16 and schedule offline calibration job
Decision heuristic must be explainable and reproducible for audits; store decision inputs in trace logs
Trade-off: running deeper on-device calibration yields better accuracy but increases cold-start time; chosen approach uses tiny sample-based checks for safety
Consider future extension: lightweight NN that predicts best path from request metadata and prompt embeddings (deferred to follow-up ticket)
Coordination needed with Console team to surface per-route fallback counts and quant-profile age
